item.title: Olivia Rodrigo Scores Career-Best Opening Week as ‘You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love’ Hits U.K. No. 1
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to this week's music update. We've got some exciting news from the UK music scene. Olivia Rodrigo is taking the top spot on the Official Albums Chart with her latest release, "You Seem Pretty Sad For a Girl So in Love".
[Short music transition]
Host: This is Rodrigo's third consecutive number one album, following "Sour" in 2021 and "Guts" in 2023. And what's even more impressive is that she's achieved the biggest opening week for an international album release in 2026, with over 103,000 chart units sold. That's double the units sold by her previous albums in their opening weeks.
[Short music transition]
Host: Rodrigo shared her thoughts on this achievement with the Official Charts Company, saying "Thank you so much for this Number 1 album award! It means so much to me... I wrote so many of these songs in the U.K., so it makes it extra special."
[Short music transition]
Host: But that's not all - other artists are also making waves on the charts. Michael Jackson's "The Essential" collection is holding strong at number 2, while Harry Styles' "Kiss All The Time. Disco, Occasionally" has jumped up to number 12. And with Styles' recent performances at London's Wembley Stadium and Meltdown Festival, his other albums, "Harry's House" and "Fine Line", are also seeing a boost in the charts.
[Short music transition]
Host: Rounding out the top 5, we have Olivia Dean's "The Art of Loving" at number 4 and Embrace's "Avalanche" at number 5, their highest position since 2018. And newcomer Sonny Fodera is making his top 20 debut with "Can We Do It All Again?" at number 20.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for this week's music update. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next one!
